assets.title: Materials fit different jobs
assets.caption: A clear window lets us see outside. A knitted sweater bends with us and can help keep us warm. Different jobs need different properties.

assets.title: Two jobs for water
assets.caption: A bead sits on one sample while water has spread into the other. These pictures illustrate different water behaviors; they do not measure how much water each material can hold.

assets.alt: A clear rounded bead sits on the left red square. The right red towel square has a dark damp patch among its loops.

assets.title: Choosing a rain cover
assets.caption: Untreated paper towel can soak through and tear when wet. That makes it a poor rain cover. Coated papers can behave differently, so name the sample you test.
assets.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Friendly simple painterly classroom illustration for Grade 2, large clear shapes, light cream background, uncluttered and accurate. A small toy bear under a miniature plain white PAPER TOWEL canopy held by a simple arch frame. Gentle water drops from above have darkened the paper and made a small tear; a few drops pass through to the toy. A tray catches water. No child in rain.
assets.alt: Water drips through a tear in a damp paper canopy onto a toy bear sitting in a tray below.

assets.title: Prepare a fair comparison
assets.caption: Compare equal-size dry samples using the same water amount, waiting time, and method. Change the sample material. Repeat with fresh dry samples.
assets.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Friendly simple painterly classroom illustration for Grade 2, large clear shapes, light cream background, uncluttered and accurate. assets.alt: Three trays hold white, blue, and green sample squares. A measuring spoon, water cup, and hourglass stand in front.

assets.title: Observe without guessing a winner
assets.caption: Notice damp areas and water still on the surface. Wet-patch size alone does not tell us which sample absorbed more. Report what you actually observe.

assets.title: Find materials around you
assets.caption: Find an object, name its job, and describe a useful property. Many objects use several materials together.

assets.alt: A kitchen contains a window showing a tree, a wooden chair, a metal pot, a white towel, and a blue bowl.

assets.title: Bending is not stretching
assets.caption: Bending changes how something curves. Stretching makes it longer. A material can bend without stretching much.
assets.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Friendly simple painterly classroom illustration for Grade 2, large clear shapes, light cream background, uncluttered and accurate. Two separate hand demonstrations side by side: left hands curve a thin blue plastic strip into an arch; right hands stretch a plain orange rubber band horizontally. Both complete visible objects, no broken ends.
assets.alt: Hands curve a blue strip into an arch at left. At right, another pair of hands pulls an orange rubber band into a long narrow loop.

assets.title: Hard does not mean unbreakable
assets.caption: Ceramic can resist dents yet chip or break. Being hard does not mean being unbreakable. An adult handles sharp or broken samples.
assets.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Friendly simple painterly classroom illustration for Grade 2, large clear shapes, light cream background, uncluttered and accurate. assets.alt: Two ceramic cups sit on a tray. The left cup is intact; the right has a chipped rim, with a detached piece beside it.

assets.title: Compare surface texture
assets.caption: Rough and smooth describe surface texture. Look closely before safely touching a sample. Texture is different from how easily it bends.
assets.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Friendly simple painterly classroom illustration for Grade 2, large clear shapes, light cream background, uncluttered and accurate. assets.alt: Two tan rectangular samples sit side by side: raised woven fibers at left and an even wooden surface with grain at right.

assets.title: Seeing through materials
assets.caption: Clear material lets you see details through it. Cloudy material lets some light through but hides details. An opaque panel blocks the view.
assets.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Friendly simple painterly classroom illustration for Grade 2, large clear shapes, light cream background, uncluttered and accurate. Behind each sits an identical red toy ball. Left panel clear so ball distinct, middle frosted translucent so ball blurry, right opaque wood entirely hides ball with no ghost showing through. No extra visible balls in front.
assets.alt: Three upright panels sit in a wooden holder. A red ball is clear through the left panel, blurred through the middle, and not visible through the wooden right panel.

assets.title: Control the sample size
assets.caption: Use a template to keep sample area the same. Keep thickness and layers alike when possible, and describe differences you cannot control.

assets.alt: Three similarly sized square samples lie in a row: white textured paper, fluffy blue fibers, and a shiny green sheet. A square white template sits above.

assets.title: Try again with fresh samples
assets.caption: Repeat the comparison using fresh dry samples. A used wet sample is a different starting condition. Similar trials make your evidence more dependable.

assets.title: Draw what you observed
assets.caption: Draw or describe what happened, including water left on top or below a sample. Keep your prediction separate from your observation.

assets.title: Use it again
assets.caption: Reusing an object gives it another job without making it into new material. Recycling is different: it processes suitable materials into new products.
